base: black-and-white editorial vintage documentary photograph, desaturated, high contrast, grainy film texture. WIDE HORIZONTAL LANDSCAPE orientation, 3:2 aspect ratio, much wider than tall. FRAMING IS CRITICAL: the camera is CLOSE and the subject is VERY LARGE, filling the entire BOTTOM THREE QUARTERS of the frame from the left edge to the right edge, extending past the bottom edge. Only a NARROW BAND across the very TOP of the frame, about one fifth of the height, is empty pale bright almost-white wall or light, completely free of objects. EVERYTHING IS IN SHARP CRISP FOCUS, deep depth of field, no blur, no bokeh, no soft focus. This is ONE single real photographic exposure, never a composite: every element shares the same light and grain. THE TOP OF THE FRAME IS BRIGHT OVEREXPOSED LIGHT, and the transition from the scene into that light is GRADUAL and soft, as if the light swallows the upper part of the scene: NO horizontal edge anywhere, no shelf edge, no ceiling line, no sign, no roofline crossing the top. Surfaces and objects fade softly upward into the light. THE TOP BAND IS A HARD REQUIREMENT: that top fifth must be ONE single continuous evenly-lit pale surface spanning the FULL width, bright and uniform, with NOTHING crossing it at all: no shelf, no beam, no lamp, no head, no edge of any object. It must read as smooth blank paper. NO fog, NO mist, NO haze and NO smoke anywhere inside the scene itself; only that narrow band at the very top is pale. Natural unposed body language. Brazil; every sign, card, notebook, photograph, uniform or object in the scene is PLAIN and UNBRANDED: no printed brand names, no logos, no legible writing of any kind; any papers, notebooks, punch cards or photographs show only vague illegible marks, never readable letters or numbers. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no emojis, no gradients, no added color, no stock photo look.
cinema: CINEMATIC DIRECTION: camera at chest height, one strong directional light source raking across the scene, deep shadows, dramatic contrast. People LARGE and CLOSE, chest up, heads at about one fifth from the top of the frame. Every person is FULLY inside the frame: heads complete with clear empty space above them, nobody cropped at the neck, shoulders or waist, nobody touching the left or right edges.
fit: COMPOSITION FOR THE SLIDE (HARD REQUIREMENT): the subject occupies ONLY the LOWER 55 percent of the frame; the ENTIRE UPPER 45 percent of the frame is a plain, flat, evenly lit surface in a very pale OFF-WHITE tone (like unbleached linen paper, hex F3F3F3), with a faint fine texture and absolutely nothing on it: no shelves, no objects, no doorway, no window, no sign, no ceiling line, no heads. That pale surface is part of the photograph and simply continues upward, staying very pale and uniform to the top edge.

images.scene: Brazil, 1970s, a small sales office. In the foreground, the BOSS seen from behind and slightly to the side, standing in an open doorway, his tense shoulders and closed fist large in the frame. Beyond him, three salesmen at their desks have stopped working and look up at him in silence, anxious, trying to read his mood. Everyone fully inside the frame.
Brazil, 1970s, CLOSE still life on a wooden office desk: two classic theater masks lying side by side, one sad (comedy and tragedy masks), next to a closed ledger and a fountain pen. NO PEOPLE.

Brazil, 1970s, CLOSE still life: an old wall tear-off calendar hanging on a nail, the top page half torn off and curling, revealing a page underneath that looks exactly the same; a few torn pages crumpled on the desk below. The pages show only vague illegible marks, no readable numbers. NO PEOPLE.

Brazil, 1970s, a simple meeting room of a small company: the OWNER, a firm middle-aged man in shirt and tie, stands at the head of a long table addressing his team of six seated salespeople, men and women, all facing him attentively, a single sheet of paper in his hand. Everyone large and fully inside the frame.

Brazil, 1970s, CLOSE still life: an old mechanical adding machine with a long paper tape curling out onto a desk, next to a pencil and a small balance scale. The paper shows only vague illegible marks, no readable numbers. NO PEOPLE.

Brazil, 1970s, a small company office: a group of coworkers standing in a loose circle, applauding a young SALESWOMAN in the center who smiles, a little embarrassed and proud; the owner beside her shakes her hand. Everyone large and fully inside the frame.

Brazil, 1970s, CLOSE still life on a wooden desk: an old brass compass, open, its needle sharp and clear, resting on top of a folded road map, with a pencil drawing a single firm line. NO PEOPLE, no readable text.

Brazil, 1970s, an office: the OWNER and a SALESMAN sit face to face across a desk, a sheet of paper between them; the owner points at one line on the sheet, serious and calm, looking the salesman in the eye; the salesman listens, attentive, not humiliated. Both large, chest up, fully inside the frame.
Brazil, 1970s, CLOSE still life: a large old brass hand bell with a wooden handle standing on a sales counter, beside an open order book and a fountain pen. NO PEOPLE.

Brazil, 1970s, CLOSE still life on a desk: a sealed brown envelope pushed to the edge of the desk, half hidden under a pile of papers, as if nobody wants to open it; a letter opener lying untouched beside it. NO PEOPLE, no readable text.
Brazil, 1970s, CLOSE still life on a wooden desk: an open notebook with handwritten lines (illegible), a fountain pen across it, and a small desk calendar. NO PEOPLE.

Brazil, 1970s, CLOSE still life: an open accounting ledger on a desk with a firm handwritten check mark next to a row (illegible lines), a fountain pen resting on it, an empty coffee cup nearby. NO PEOPLE.
